title: “Success" is one of those words that seems simple until you try to define it. There's no single answer—it means different things to different people, and even to the same person at different stages of life. Here are the main ways people understand it: 1. Achievement of goals The most common definition: setting a target and reaching it. A promotion, a degree, a marathon, a business launch. This view is measurable and concrete. 2. Happiness and contentment Some argue that if you're not happy, no external achievement counts as success. In this view, success is a felt state, not a trophy. 3. Meaning and purpose Viktor Frankl, who survived the Holocaust, argued that success follows meaning rather than the reverse: "Don't aim at success—the more you aim at it and make it a target, the more you are going to miss it." Success here is living in alignment with what matters to you. 4. Impact on others For many, success means contributing—raising healthy children, helping a community, creating something useful. It's measured by what you give, not what you get. 5. Resilience and growth Some define success as simply continuing—learning from failure, becoming a slightly better version of yourself over time. Under this view, failure isn't the opposite of success; it's part of it. 6. Societal definition (the one to be cautious about) Much of what we call success is culturally programmed: money, status, fame, titles. These are external and comparative—there's always someone richer or more famous, so this definition tends to produce anxiety rather than satisfaction. #moodboard #success #manifestation #motivation #blowthisup
